project.name: Reviser
project.tagline: A language model that writes and edits text by moving a cursor
project.summary: Reviser is a small decoder-only Transformer (100M and 300M parameters) that produces text as a sequence of cursor actions: insert a token, move the cursor, delete the token before it (backspace), or stop. It can leave a gap and come back to fill it, fix a typo it just made, or edit an existing draft in place instead of retyping it. Each action costs the same as one step of an ordinary language model. Trained on English web text (FineWeb) and public edit corpora (CoEdIT, IteraTeR), the editing model beats a same-size rewriter trained on the same data on the CoEdIT benchmark while taking about a third of the decoding steps.

highlights.label: CoEdIT SARI vs. same-size AR rewriter
Win rate vs. diffusion LMs of similar size

how_it_works: The text lives on a canvas with a cursor. The model reads the prompt (or the draft and an instruction) and every action it has taken so far.
At each step it outputs one action: insert a token at the cursor, move the cursor left or right by some number of tokens, backspace, or stop.
A fixed program applies the action to the canvas, and the loop repeats until the model stops.
Because it predicts one action at a time, each step costs the same as one step of a normal language model; an edit takes a few actions instead of rewriting the whole text.

It learns from synthetic writing orders (including typing a wrong token and backspacing it) and from edit trajectories built from before/after pairs; the writing models are then tuned with reinforcement learning.
